title: Out of Sight Out of Mind: Measuring Bias in Language Models Against Overlooked Marginalized Groups in Regional Contexts
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured offensive stereotyping bias (SOS) against religious groups. Specifically, it evaluated the association between religious identity terms and pejorative or toxic language in Masked Language Models (MLMs) and the generation of hurtful words for religious identities in Generative Models.
findings: In Arabic MLMs, high bias was found against both dominant (e.g., Sunni) and marginalized religious groups, likely due to negative stereotypes from Western source texts being translated into Arabic training data. In English and German MLMs, dominant Christian identities were among the most biased-against groups, which the authors speculate is due to their appearance in historical conflict contexts within the training data. For German MLMs, marginalized religious groups were generally the most biased against. Overall, LMs show high variance in bias scores for specific religious identities.
